ScreenSwap
==========

Swaps everything between your two monitors with one keystroke.

Whatever is on the left screen goes to the right, and whatever is on the
right comes to the left. Maximised windows stay maximised. Minimised
windows stay minimised. Nothing else changes.

    Press:  Ctrl + Alt + X


HOW TO START IT
---------------

Double-click ScreenSwap.exe.

Nothing appears to happen. That's correct. It puts a small icon in the
system tray, down near the clock, and waits. Press Ctrl+Alt+X to use it.

If the icon isn't next to the clock, click the little "^" arrow there to
show hidden icons. You can drag it out onto the taskbar to keep it visible.


WINDOWS WILL WARN YOU. THIS IS NORMAL.
--------------------------------------

The first time you run it, you'll probably see a blue box:

    "Windows protected your PC"

This is not a virus warning. It appears for every program that hasn't
been signed with a paid certificate, which costs a few hundred dollars a
year and isn't worth it for a small free tool. Windows shows this for all
new, unsigned software regardless of what it does.

To run it anyway:

    1. Click "More info"
    2. Click "Run anyway"

You'll only need to do this once.

If you'd rather not trust an .exe from someone else, that's completely
reasonable. The full source code is included as ScreenSwap.cs, it's about
1,500 lines of readable C#, and build.cmd rebuilds the .exe using the
compiler already built into Windows. You can read exactly what it does
and compile it yourself.


THE TRAY MENU
-------------

Right-click the tray icon:

  Swap screens now          Same as pressing the hotkey
  Swap and show report      Swaps, then shows exactly what it moved
  Tray icon                 16 icon designs to pick from
  Icon colour               Auto, always white, or always black
  Start with Windows        Tick this to have it launch automatically
  Open log file             What it has been doing
  Exit                      Quits

Double-clicking the tray icon also swaps.


THINGS WORTH KNOWING
--------------------

* It needs two monitors. With one, it tells you there's nothing to swap.
  With three or more, it swaps the leftmost and rightmost and leaves
  anything in between alone.

* Windows that are running as administrator will not move. Windows itself
  blocks this, and there is nothing a normal program can do about it. If
  a window stubbornly stays put, that's why.

* Your monitors don't have to be the same size or resolution. Windows are
  scaled proportionally, so a half-width window stays half-width.

* It uses about 30 MB of memory and no CPU at all when idle.


IF SOMETHING GOES WRONG
-----------------------

Right-click the tray icon and choose "Open log file". It records every
start, every swap, and any error.

To see what it WOULD do without it touching anything, open a Command
Prompt in this folder and run:

    ScreenSwap.exe /dryrun

That writes a report listing every window it can see, which screen it
thinks each one is on, and where it would move it. It changes nothing.


UNINSTALLING
------------

There is no installer, so there's nothing to uninstall.

  1. Right-click the tray icon and choose Exit
  2. If you ticked "Start with Windows", untick it first
  3. Delete this folder

It leaves behind two small things you can ignore or remove:
  - a log folder at  %LOCALAPPDATA%\ScreenSwap
  - your icon choice in the registry at  HKCU\Software\ScreenSwap


Requires Windows 10 or 11. No installation, no dependencies, no internet
access, no telemetry. It does not phone home and never touches the network.
